title: Isolated eval pipelines for private & dedicated deployments
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments need regression checks that run whenever model binaries or serving configs change, but they require strict data isolation and proof that PII and customer data never leave their environment. Current eval infra is multi-tenant and uses shared datasets/configs, which is incompatible with several enterprise customers' compliance requirements.

Goal: Provide an opt-in feature that runs customer-specific eval suites in an isolated environment (either in-customer VPC or isolated tenant within Dedicated) whenever model or config changes are proposed for rollout. The system must: (1) execute the evals without exporting customer data, (2) store results and artifacts under the customer's control (or encrypted with customer KMS), (3) produce gated decisions (pass/fail/block rollout) based on configurable thresholds, and (4) emit audit logs and signed provenance for compliance reviews.

Scope: MVP will support: (a) eval execution in a customer-controlled runner (containerized Kubernetes Job / Fargate) for Private customers or in logically isolated nodes for Dedicated customers, (b) configurable eval suites per customer (upload/declare set of prompts + metrics), (c) secret-backed KMS integration for encrypting results, and (d) a rollout-gate webhook for the deployment pipeline that blocks if thresholds are not met.

Non-goals: Building an automatic dataset anonymizer for arbitrary datasets (we will provide pattern-based PII masking and recommend synthetic dataset guidance), and supporting federated evals across multiple customer accounts in MVP.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customers can register an eval suite (JSON manifest + optional dataset) into their Private/Dedicated control plane UI or via API.
- Eval runner executes inside customer network boundary and reports metrics to the customer's encrypted results store.
- Platform exposes a rollout-gate endpoint that returns pass/fail and a signed summary; deployment automation can consume this to halt or continue a rollout.
- All eval artifacts are encrypted with the customer's KMS key (or stored only in-customer when Private).
- Audit trail generated for each run with who/what/when, and links to stored artifacts.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Runner placement: prefer in-customer runner for Private customers (highest isolation) and isolated tenant pools for Dedicated (faster onboarding). Trade-off: Private runners increase operational complexity and support scope; Dedicated isolation reduces complexity but requires strict scheduling guarantees.
- Data handling: Allow customers to upload test datasets or point to internal stores (S3/GCS) that the runner can access; we will support pattern-based PII masking and an optional synthetic-data recommendation checklist. Full DP/federated approaches are out-of-scope for MVP.
- Thresholds & metrics: Default metrics set (perplexity delta, n-gram overlap, hallucination rate as measured by reference checks) but customers can supply custom metric hooks.
- Cost/latency: Running customer-specific suites per model change can be expensive; provide policy options: run on every model/config change (strict), run only on major model versions (balanced), or run daily snapshots (cost-savings).

Security & compliance controls:
- Must support customer KMS/HSM key identifiers for encrypting results.
- Runner credentials are ephemeral, rotated per job, and never persist in control plane logs.
- Results metadata includes SHA256 of model binary and config; signed by Redwood service for provenance.
- Security review will be required prior to GA.

Deliverables:
- API: POST /customers/:id/eval-suites (manifest + dataset reference), GET run status, GET signed summary
- UI: Console flows to create eval suites, view recent runs, configure thresholds, and link to audit logs
- Infra: Customer-runner container image, helm chart + minimal operator to bootstrap in-customer jobs, and a lightweight agent for Dedicated isolation pools
- Docs: Confluence deployment guide, security FAQ, runbook for failure modes

Success metrics:
- 5 pilot customers onboarded within 3 months of MVP launch
- <2 false positive blocks in first 10k eval runs (tunable thresholds)
- Customers report being able to validate model changes without manual data exports (customer survey).
comments: 2025-11-04: Kickoff with PM, Eng, and Security. Agreed MVP scope and target customers for pilot (two Private, one Dedicated). Action: Eng to draft runner design and security checklist. - Anika

2025-11-06: Eng design review. Marco proposed a containerized eval-runner that mounts customer S3 via short-lived credentials; Security pushed back and requested KMS-wrapped credentials and ephemeral mounts. Decision: implement KMS-wrapped temporary creds and ephemeral filesystem. - Marco

2025-11-07: UX sketch review with Design. Elena suggested adding an "impact preview" that shows estimated cost and run time before scheduling a suite. PM accepted as low-priority enhancement for MVP. - Elena

2025-11-10: Security review kickoff notes added to Confluence (link below). Primary risk: leakage via runner logs. Mitigation: redact logs by default and store full logs only in customer-controlled storage. - Priya (Security)

2025-11-12: Narrowed metrics for MVP to: perplexity delta, response-time regressed p99, and hallucination rate (simple reference-check). Marco to spin up prototype runner in test VPC next week. - Anika
